title: Diocletian Divides the Empire
objective: After this level you can explain Diocletian's reforms and the Tetrarchy.
summary: Diocletian ended the crisis in 284 CE with four emperors, smaller provinces and price controls, then retired to his palace at Split.

cards.headline: One emperor wasn’t enough. Diocletian tried four.
Rule of four
cards.body: Diocletian became emperor in 284 CE and ended the half century of crisis. He created the Tetrarchy, “rule of four”: two senior emperors, called Augusti, and two junior ones, called Caesars. It was meant to put an emperor near every threatened frontier and give the empire a planned succession.
cards.callout: Tetrarchy: two Augusti and two Caesars

cards.headline: Reforms
cards.body: Diocletian split the provinces into smaller units and separated civil from military command. In 301 CE his Edict on Maximum Prices tried, and failed, to stop inflation by fixing prices.

cards.fact: Diocletian did what no emperor had done: he retired.
cards.context: In 305 CE he stepped down voluntarily and moved to his palace at Split, in modern Croatia.
